**Get last year's LIMS sample data from Nivabasen**    

* Just the sample data,not the concentrations - one row per sample  

* Filtering and joining is done using lazy table loading    
    - "Lazy" means that the data are not actually downloaded until you use 'collect()'  
    - So, if you wait using collect() until you have done the filtering, you avoid downloading unnecessary data  

* This script accesses Nivabasen on Oracle and therefore needs your Oracle user name (your initials) and password. It can be run in two ways:  
    - Interactively - run chunk by chunk (by clicking the little arrow in the corner of the chunk, or Shift+Ctrl+Enter and Shift-Alt-N) - enter username and password when you are asked for it 
    - Or by using "Knit with Parameters..." from the menu (pull-down menu from the Knit button) - enter username and password, then click 'Knit'  

## 1. Libraries

```{r}

# For loading libraries without startup messages
library2 <- function(...) suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(...))

library2(dbplyr)
library2(dplyr)
library2(lubridate)
library2(ggplot2)
library2(stringr)
library2(knitr)

source("083_functions.R")

# help(package = "dbplyr")

```

## 2. Settings  
```{r}

measurement_year <- 2025

# Set to TRUE if you want to download the data (ca. 6 minutes)
download_and_save <- TRUE

```



## 3. Set up Oracle connection   

- This part of the script will ask you about your user name and password to Nivabasen  

```{r}

con <- create_connection()

```

## 4. Set up queries  

* These define how to get data from Nivabasen, but don't actually get them  


### Get pointers to tables  

```{r}

projects <- tbl(con, in_schema("NIVADATABASE", "LABWARE_CHECK_SAMPLE")) %>%
  count(ACCOUNT_NUMBER, PROSJEKT, CUSTOMER)

samples <- tbl(con, in_schema("NIVADATABASE", "LABWARE_CHECK_SAMPLE"))

```

## 5. Get samples  

### List projects 

```{r}

projects %>% 
  filter(upper(CUSTOMER) %in% 'MSC') %>%
  show_query()
# All Merete's projects  
dat_projects <- projects %>%
  filter(upper(CUSTOMER) %in% 'MSC') %>%
  collect()

# View(dat_projects)

```

### Get samples for all years    

* Download should take around 20 seconds  

```{r}

project <- "O 210200.ANAIN"
cat("Name of project:", project, " \n\n")

labware_sample_all <- samples %>%
  filter(PROSJEKT %in% project) %>%
  collect()

# labware_sample_all_back <- labware_sample_all
```


### b2. Check samples with conflicting year info    

* In some cases, year in SAMPLED_DATE is different from year in TEXT_ID

#### Data for checking  

```{r}
# All years
df_check_years <- labware_sample_all %>%
  mutate(
    year_sample = year(SAMPLED_DATE),
    month_sample = month(SAMPLED_DATE),
    year_textid = as.numeric(substr(TEXT_ID, 4, 7)))
xtabs(~year_sample + year_textid, df_check_years)
```

#### Conficting year information
```{r}
# Check those with conflicting year info  
df_check_year_conflicts <- df_check_years %>%
  # Select those where year in SAMPLED_DATE is different from year in TEXT_ID  
  filter(year_sample != year_textid) %>%
  select(SAMPLED_DATE, TEXT_ID, year_sample, month_sample, year_textid,
         DESCRIPTION, AQUAMONITOR_CODE, TISSUE)

xtabs(~year_sample + year_textid, df_check_year_conflicts)

```

#### Check  
```{r}

cat("-----------------------------------------------\n")
cat("One of the year info is", measurement_year, "or", 
    measurement_year+1, "\n-----------------------------------------------\n")

df_check1 <- df_check_year_conflicts %>%
  filter(
    year_sample %in% c(measurement_year, measurement_year+1) | 
      year_textid == c(measurement_year, measurement_year+1)) %>%
  # Does DESCRIPTION contain 'blank'?  
  mutate(
    blank = grepl("blank", DESCRIPTION, ignore.case = TRUE))

xtabs(~year_sample + year_textid, df_check1)

xtabs(~addNA(AQUAMONITOR_CODE) + paste0(year_sample, ",", year_textid), df_check1)

```

### Excluding blank samples (DESCRIPTION contains 'blank')

```{r}

cat("-----------------------------------------------\n")
cat("2023 - exclude blanks\n-----------------------------------------------\n")

xtabs(~year_sample + year_textid, df_check1)                    #ELU: skal det være df_check1 her? får feilmelding

xtabs(~addNA(AQUAMONITOR_CODE) + paste0(year_sample, ",", year_textid), df_check1)            #ELU: skal det være df_check1 her? får feilmelding

```

### Including SAMPLED_DATE     
Conclusion:
* 28A2 are samples taken in January 2026, belonging to the "sample year" 2025 (1. Feb 2025-31. Jan 2026) -> this is OK
* 33F are old samples from flatfish colleced in previous years, analysed this year  
```{r}
df_check1 %>%             #ELU: skal det være df_check1 her? får feilmelding
  count(AQUAMONITOR_CODE, SAMPLED_DATE, TISSUE, year_textid, year_sample) %>%
  kable()

```


### b3. Get 'labware_sample'   

* From code above, we found that we can download all samples where either year in SAMPLED_DATE or year in TEXT_ID is `measurement_year` (or both)   

```{r}

labware_samples <- labware_sample_all %>%
  filter(
    # year(SAMPLED_DATE) == 2023 | as.numeric(substr(TEXT_ID, 4, 7)) == 2023) %>%
    year(SAMPLED_DATE) == measurement_year | as.numeric(substr(TEXT_ID, 4, 7)) == measurement_year) %>%
  collect()

# Exlude blanks
labware_samples <- labware_samples %>%
  filter(
    !grepl("blank", DESCRIPTION, ignore.case = TRUE)) 

# make timestamp to use in file name (NOTE: UTC = Greenwich mean time used, not local time)
now <- lubridate::now()
timestring <- paste0(substr(now, 1, 10), "_", substr(now, 12, 13), "h", substr(now, 15, 16), "m")  

cat("-----------------------------------------------\n")
cat("Number of samples -", measurement_year, "(excluding blanks)\n-----------------------------------------------\n")
nrow(labware_samples)

```

## 6. Save   

```{r}

# Needs only be save if different from previously downloaded data

fn_rds <- paste0("83_Labware_samples_", measurement_year, "_", timestring, ".rds")  
fn_csv <- sub(".rds", ".csv", fn_rds)  

# fn_rds; fn_csv
saveRDS(labware_samples, paste0("Input_data/", fn_rds))
readr::write_csv(labware_samples, paste0("Input_data/", fn_csv), na = "")
  
message("Data saved to 'Input_data' as ", sQuote(fn_csv), " (and as a corresponding .rds file)")

# all years
fn_rds <- paste0("83_Labware_samples_all_", timestring, ".rds")  
fn_csv <- sub(".rds", ".csv", fn_rds)  
readr::write_csv(labware_sample_all, paste0("Input_data/", fn_csv), na = "")
message("Data saved to 'Input_data' as ", sQuote(fn_csv), " (and as a corresponding .rds file)")
  

```

## 7. APPENDIX: data  

### Example  
```{r}

if (FALSE){
  dir("Input_data", pattern = "83_Labware_samples_2024")
  labware_samples <- readRDS("Input_data/83_Labware_samples_2024_2025-08-27_13h41m.rds")
}

textid_sel <- labware_samples %>% 
  filter(AQUAMONITOR_CODE == "30B" & SPECIES == "Gadus morhua" & TISSUE == "LI-Lever") %>% 
  pull(TEXT_ID) %>% 
  sort()

import <- tbl(con, in_schema("NIVADATABASE", "LABWARE_IMPORT"))

import_sel <- import %>% 
  filter(TEXT_ID == "NR-2024-08136") %>% 
  collect()

table(import_sel$T_ANALYSIS_METHOD)
table(import_sel$PARAM)

```

### Getting lacking PAH metabolites, 2024  
```{r}

samples_sel <- labware_samples %>% 
  filter(AQUAMONITOR_CODE %in% c("15B", "53B", "23B") & SPECIES == "Gadus morhua" & TISSUE == "BI-Galle")
  
textid_sel <- samples_sel %>% 
  pull(TEXT_ID) %>% 
  sort()

import <- tbl(con, in_schema("NIVADATABASE", "LABWARE_IMPORT"))

import_sel <- import %>% 
  filter(TEXT_ID %in% textid_sel) %>% 
  collect()

table(import_sel$T_ANALYSIS_METHOD)
table(import_sel$PARAM)

if (FALSE){
  saveRDS(import_sel, "Input_data/Biological_effects_cod/2024/083_PAH_metabolites_15B-53B-23B.rds")
  saveRDS(samples_sel, "Input_data/Biological_effects_cod/2024/083_PAH_metabolites_15B-53B-23B_samples.rds")
}

```

### Milfersk 2024 checking  

Suspicious results in Vannmiljø export
* Number of BRPFOS (branched PFOS) results are 2x that of other PFAS   
* L5 (slioxan) lacking for one sample?  
* 

#### table pointers  
```{r}

create_table_pointers()     # creates the dbplyr objects 'lims_projects' and 'lims_samples'

```

#### get samples  
```{r}

# Projects  
dat_projects <- lims_projects %>%
  # filter(grepl("MILFERSK", PROSJEKT, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%  # doesn't work
  filter(sql("PROSJEKT like '%210136%'")) %>%                    # works
  collect()

projects <- pull(dat_projects, PROSJEKT)

df_lims_samples <- lims_samples %>%
  filter(PROSJEKT %in% projects) %>% 
  filter(year(SAMPLED_DATE) == 2024) %>% # show_query()
  collect()

table(df_lims_samples$AQUAMONITOR_CODE)
table(df_lims_samples$TISSUE)

# example (trout liver from Mjøsa)
# . get TEXT_ID
textid <- df_lims_samples %>% 
  filter(AQUAMONITOR_CODE == "Ørret_M" & TISSUE == "LI-Lever") %>% 
  head(1) %>% 
  pull(TEXT_ID)

import_test1 <- lims_import %>%
  filter(TEXT_ID %in% textid) %>%
  collect()

```


#### get all data   
- from all samples  

```{r}
# All samples
textid_all <- labware_sample_all %>% 
  pull(TEXT_ID)

# All samples with PFOS (and therefore all PFAS)
df_limsdata <- lims_import %>%
  filter(TEXT_ID %in% textid_all) %>%
  collect()
```

#### check PFAS   
- seems ok, including for brPFOS   
```{r}

if (FALSE){
df_limsdata %>%
  filter(REPORTED_NAME %in% par_pfas) %>%
  xtabs(~ REPORTED_NAME + DESCRIPTION, .)
}

# boring plot
df_limsdata %>%
  filter(REPORTED_NAME %in% par_pfas) %>%
  distinct(REPORTED_NAME, DESCRIPTION, ENTRY_QUALIFIER) %>%
  ggplot(aes(DESCRIPTION, REPORTED_NAME, fill = is.na(ENTRY_QUALIFIER))) +
  geom_tile() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = -45, hjust = 0))

```
